Class ColumnStructure

Namespace
ParquetNeo.Nested
Assembly
ParquetNeo.dll

The shape of the data in one column, as validity and offsets instead of definition and repetition levels: for each optional node on the way to the column whether its value is present, and for each repeated node where each list starts and ends. It is the columnar form of nested data (the same idea as the validity and offsets of an Arrow array), and it converts both ways with the levels the reader returns and the writer takes.

Remarks

Only the nodes that can be missing or repeated take part; required nodes add nothing. The Levels come outermost first. Every level has one entry per item of its depth: depth 0 has one item per row, and the items of depth d are the elements of the d-th repeated level. Where an ancestor is missing, the entries of the optional levels below it (at the same depth) say false and a repeated level below it says an empty list.

The values of the column are not part of the structure: they are the values of the entries whose every ancestor is present, in order, which is exactly what ColumnWriter takes and ColumnReader returns.

Remarks

A batch of a repeated column can end in the middle of a row. The entries from the last one with repetition level 0 on may be the start of a row that goes on in the next batch, so assemble only the entries before them and carry the rest over. At the end of the column the whole batch is complete.
